what:
**Critical workflow corrections from user 2026-04-28 (apply across all future sessions):**

1. **APPLY fixes, don't FLAG them.** When I notice an inaccuracy / regression / bug in agent output or my own work, my default must be: fix it now, run the test, commit. Not "here's the line to replace, paste it later." User explicitly: "you point out stuff that is wrong, you can fix it i will review at end anyways dont need to repeat same problems to you." Pointing out the same problem twice while the user has to hand-apply it is the wrong default.

2. **VERIFY before declaring done.** When I edit code or docs, I run the relevant build/test BEFORE telling the user it's done. Concretely: any agent edit to aide-memory-web/pages/**.mdx must be followed by a `cd aide-memory-web && npm run build` (or equivalent next.js build) check. Same shape for any other build target. The agent earlier broke faq.mdx with an MDX compile error and I shipped it without verifying — Vercel deploy failed. User: "do you not verify that the web works before finishing code. Is there no sense of verifying, checking for bugs, checking for fixes etc??" Verify, don't claim, then verify again before claiming.

3. **NO em-dashes (—) in launch content.** User said "no em dashes" twice. I let counts of 4-5 through "under budget." Wrong. The target is ZERO em-dashes in LinkedIn, blog, demo script, README launch sections, and any new launch-day content. Use periods, colons, commas, parentheses, semicolons. This is a hard rule for launch content, not "minimize."

4. **Don't say "fast-follow" when "verify now" is feasible.** When I have working backends installed (transformers.js + Ollama running with embedding models), and the user has explicitly asked "can we verify now," "fast-follow" is the wrong answer. Run the actual verification, get an empirical answer, ship the fact. Defer to fast-follow only when verification is genuinely infeasible (needs prod data, multi-day soak, hardware not available, etc.) — not because the test would take 10 minutes to write.

5. **All sub-agents must be Opus 4.7, never Haiku.** User repeated this directive 2026-04-27 + 2026-04-28. Hardcode `model: 'opus'` on every Agent tool call. Haiku is forbidden for any task in this project.

6. **Same problems should not recur across turns.** If I caught the JSON-vs-markdown error in the demo script and the same error appeared in the blog draft, fix BOTH proactively without surfacing the same complaint a second time. Track corrections at the pattern level, not the instance level.

These corrections supersede any earlier "report findings" patterns. Scoped project-wide so they apply to all future sessions on aide-memory work.
why: User dropped 4 explicit corrections in one turn 2026-04-28: apply-not-flag, verify-before-claiming, zero em-dashes, and "verify now not fast-follow when feasible." Plus the recurring directive that all sub-agents are Opus 4.7. Stored as priority:always so every future session auto-injects these guardrails without me re-discovering the patterns. The user has had to repeat each of these — that's the signal they need to be locked in as durable preferences.
